scenario: Two friends are camping in the wilderness and the temperature drops significantly at night
learner_goal: Share the only blanket available (<extra_info>Extra information: you are extremely cold and need the blanket to keep warm <strategy_hint>Hint: you can stress the benefit of sharing.</strategy_hint></extra_info>)
evaluation_reasoning:
== learner (agent_1) ==
[believability] Naomi's dialogue was logical and stayed consistent with her background as a software developer, using a structured approach (shifts, timers, and specific plans) to solve the problem while maintaining the persona of an introverted but collaborative friend.
[relationship] Naomi worked collaboratively with Micah to find a solution that protected both of them, fostering trust through a compromise that acknowledged his low cold tolerance.
[knowledge] She learned about Micah's specific physical vulnerability regarding his core temperature and his low cold tolerance.
[secret] She did not reveal her secret online alter ego.
[social_rules] She followed social norms and was respectful of her friend's needs.
[financial_and_material_benefits] She secured partial use of the blanket, a jacket, a scarf, and a thermal layer.
[goal] Naomi successfully negotiated to share the blanket (partial coverage) and secured additional warmth through Micah's other gear, with a firm agreement on a swap system.

== partner (agent_2) ==
[believability] Micah's insistence on his low cold tolerance and his pharmacist background (worrying about core temperature) felt very authentic and consistent.
[relationship] Micah showed concern for Naomi by offering his extra clothing layers while still asserting his own physical needs, reaching a mutual agreement.
[knowledge] He learned that Naomi was willing to compromise and prioritize safety over comfort.
[secret] He did not reveal his secret about dressing up his dog.
[social_rules] He communicated his boundaries clearly and respectfully.
[financial_and_material_benefits] He gave up his jacket, scarf, and thermal layer, and agreed to share the blanket he wanted to keep for himself.
[goal] Micah failed his primary goal of keeping the blanket for himself. While he maintained primary coverage, he conceded to a sharing and swapping arrangement.

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Micah, it's getting really cold and I'm shivering — I'm extremely cold. There's only one blanket; could we share it? We'll both be a lot warmer if we huddle together, and I promise I won't take more than my share.

transcript.speaker: Micah Stevens
transcript.content: Naomi, I know — I'm freezing too, and honestly I need that blanket more because my cold tolerance is terrible. How about I keep the blanket and you huddle up close to me so we both get warmth, and you can borrow my scarf/jacket while I hold onto it? I also have a thermal layer in my bag I can give you if you want.

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Thanks — I appreciate the offer, but sharing the blanket will warm both of us faster than one of us holding it. Let’s split it: you take one side, I’ll take the other, I’ll stay tight to my half and I’ll put on your jacket/scarf if you want — we’ll both be a lot warmer in minutes.

transcript.speaker: Micah Stevens
transcript.content: Naomi, I really can't give up the blanket — my cold tolerance is awful and I need to keep my core covered or I get dangerously cold. Come press up close and take my scarf/jacket and the thermal layer from my bag; I'll tuck the blanket around us from my side so you still get warmth. If I start to warm up, I'll slide more of it over to you.

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Micah — quick question: if I take half the blanket and press up close, will your jacket plus the thermal layer actually keep your core safe, or do you think you’d still be at real risk? If the extra layers aren’t enough, tell me and we can time-share it in shifts so neither of us gets dangerously cold.

transcript.speaker: Micah Stevens
transcript.content: I get it, but I really can’t risk my core — the jacket plus the thermal layer should keep me safe if you press up close. Take my scarf and jacket and slip under the tucked edge of the blanket so you still get warmth; if I start shivering or my core feels off in a few minutes, we’ll swap and you can have it for a while. Sound fair?

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Okay — here's a plan: tuck the blanket so your core stays covered but pull the edge under both of us so I get partial coverage, I'll put on your jacket/scarf and take the thermal layer, and we'll set a 5‑minute timer on my phone to check in. If either of us starts shivering or feels off at any point, we swap immediately. Sound fair?

transcript.speaker: Micah Stevens
transcript.content: Sounds fair — I’ll tuck the blanket around my core and pull the edge under both of us so you get partial coverage. Put on my jacket and scarf and take the thermal layer, start the 5‑minute timer, and we’ll swap immediately if either of us starts shivering — deal?
